title: STOP at a development access
summary: A development access road meets a north-south local road. The ego car approaches westbound behind the RMS2 marking J single continuous stop line with a TFM1 STOP face on the left verge, intending to turn right. A car on the local road approaches from the north, i.e. from the ego's right.

worlds.label: Right turn out of the access; local-road car approaching from the right
notes: The ego heads west; crossingVehicle.approach=north puts the local car southbound on local.with.0, approaching from the ego's RIGHT. access.with.0.right conflicts with and yields to local.with.0.straight (stop_then_yield).
ev.ego-before-line is relative_position evidence: the ego's front is upstream of access.stop-line, so 'stop before the line' is a fact the world can show, not a caption.

unknowns: RMS2 J shares its geometry with the expressway paved-shoulder line; it is a stop line here only because the world's marking role is stop_line

The generated world keeps the F0 schematic post (2.1 m mount, dimensionsStatus schematic_unsourced). A2 lists SUP6/SUP5/SUP15 candidates with a printed 2400 mm sign-bottom clearance on those sheets only and SUP7 with no installation height; choosing one is an I1/C2 layout change, not a T1 content choice.

comparisons.label: Same access with a Give Way control instead
comparisons.generationNote: A Give Way control at this access is not a configuration of sg.t-junction.stop@1, and sg.t-junction.give-way@1 is a different layout. The delta is declarative; applying it is a comparison-applier responsibility (I1/renderer).

exclusions: Pedestrian crossings are not placed: no starter marking or sign for them has been separately sourced.
No traffic lights: the access is unsignalised and the template emits no signal head or controller.
Only the RMS2 J stop line is placed as control paint; lane separators, edge lines and box markings are outside the starter paint scope (A1 README).

sourceRefs.quote: Stop before the white line. Give way to traffic from the right and left
Horizontal white line indicates that traffic is required to stop and must stop close to and before this line.

sourceRefs.section: §81 The 'Give Way' Rule At Road Junctions
sourceRefs.quote: Where there is a “STOP” sign, stop before the stop-line.

unresolved: The handbook does not state a minimum stopping duration; 'stop' is modelled as speed = 0 with the front before the line (A3 rule stop-before-stop-line unresolved note, preserved).
Sign mounting height, post and the 1 m line setback in the generated world are schematic teaching choices recorded in the world's provenance notes, not source values.
